proposals.relationship: Genovese draws on Woodward’s account of intertwined Black and Southern cultures and credits his indispensable advice and criticism.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Roll, Jordan, Roll preface quotes Woodward’s American Counterpoint on mutually shaped Black and Southern cultures; the acknowledgments call his encouragement, advice and criticism indispensable. This is a specific intellectual framing and critical resource, not certification of Genovese’s nationality thesis, formal mentorship, or a fresh reading of Woodward’s whole book. Later criticism of Genovese’s paternalism remains intact.

proposals.relationship: Genovese credits Davis with sharing ideas and helping revise Roll, Jordan, Roll section by section.
proposals.evidence_note: The acknowledgments describe Davis, concurrently resident at Stanford, reading the manuscript section by section, sharing ideas and helping over rough spots while writing his own book. This supports a substantive intellectual and revision contribution, not coauthorship or agreement with every conclusion. Existing reverse Genovese→Davis resource edge_1866 and Davis→Genovese political critique edge_1867 remain unchanged.

proposals.relationship: Genovese gives qualified support to Du Bois’s claim that exploitation intensified in slavery’s final decade.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Farmers, Planters, and Overseers, paragraph beginning Contrary to legend, gives SOME credence to Du Bois’s exploitation claim in light of a dip in reproduction rates, immediately qualifying this with if so and denying overseers full or primary responsibility. This records Genovese’s particular argumentative use, not independently verified demography or wholesale endorsement of Du Bois. The permitted public preview is unpaginated; adjacent notes 34–35 do not expose the terminal reference. No exact Du Bois work is inferred from the separate Black Reconstruction permissions list.
